conventions.convention: The metric is diag(−1,1,1,1), Box = −∂t² + Δx, and μ ≥ 0 is an inverse-length mathematical shell parameter.
Hμ uses the mode exp(−iωμ|t|)/(2ωμ), spatial Fourier measure d³k/(2π)³, and no extra prefactor i; its Green source is +iδ0.

Scalar backgrounds are smooth and real; spinor backgrounds are smooth commuting complex fields. Variations have compact support. Action notation denotes finite first variations without assuming globally integrable backgrounds.
Countable Choice is assumed. Fock inner products are second-variable-linear; tempered-distribution pairings are complex bilinear without conjugating tests.

Scalar mathematical spatial generators use dΓ(−kj). Finite variance requires a normalized vector in D(A), whereas AB requires a vector in D(B) whose B-image lies in D(A); D(A²) is not required for variance.

Scalar point-limit divergence assumes both Schwartz distributional convergence and almost-everywhere shell-Fourier convergence. The sufficient concentration condition includes bounded L1 norms. Dirac point-limit divergence concerns equal-time operator norm for a nonzero limiting spinor.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the fixed scalar shell conventions with μ ≥ 0. The displayed partial spatial Fourier formula defines a tempered Hμ, equals Wμ on t > 0 and Wμ(−t,−x) on t < 0, is symmetric under simultaneous coordinate reversal, agrees with both orderings on spacelike-separated supports, and satisfies (Box − μ²)Hμ = iδ0 without an extra prefactor i.

Under Countable Choice and the cited free-field hypotheses, real scalar smearings have self-adjoint closures on the supplied Segal domains; scalar and Dirac translation generators have their exact maximal multiplier domains; normalized vectors in D(A) have finite mean and variance without requiring D(A²). Scalar point approximations satisfying the stated distributional and shell-Fourier limits have divergent vacuum-vector norms. Equal-time Dirac smearings converging distributionally to a nonzero spinor point mass have divergent operator norms.

For the stated smooth real scalar and smooth commuting complex spinor backgrounds, the normalized densities have finite compactly supported first variations δSφ = ∫h(Box − μ²)φ and δSD = 2 Re ∫χ†β(iγa∂a − μ)ψ. Stationarity under all admissible variations holds if and only if the respective pointwise equations hold; the adjoint Dirac equation follows.

alerts.finding: The Statement identifies Ψt(u) as the equal-time field defined in lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality, then says 'For each fixed coordinate time t in seconds'. That supplier defines Ψt using WD(t,k), whose parameter t is a length-coordinate increment in def-qft-dirac-projections. With x0 = ct, the physical-time expression needs the parameter conversion Ψct or an explicit reparameterization. The divergence conclusion survives this conversion, but the displayed supplier use mixes time units.

seams_checked.note: The action lemma uses the exact Dirac blocks and adjoint. The domain lemma preserves the projected CAR space, bounded smearing, equal-time CAR, and maximal translation-generator domains, including Countable Choice and draft-supplier qualifications.

The adopted action cites the compact-variation identities with commuting spinors and no global integrability assumption. Observable definitions preserve exact domains and explicitly distinguish physical +ℏkj momentum from the mathematical −kj spatial generator.

The domain and correspondence consumers preserve the finite-variance and composition-domain conditions, compact classical variations, and the distinction between classical equations and separately adopted Fock representations. The point-profile claims are proved directly as well; the equal-time parameter-unit wording is separately alerted.

The charged-current lemma uses the free compact-variation and matrix-adjoint interface faithfully. It supplies its charged multiplication terms and localization on an arbitrary open U locally, rather than attributing those extensions to the free-action supplier.

Formal time ordering preserves Hμ's symmetry, no-prefactor-i convention, positive-time ordering, and spacelike agreement. Causal factorization uses those equalities on an open neighborhood of the separated support product and retains its regular-functional, coefficientwise formal scope.
